_README: Cross-mission Apollo anomaly scenario set for the §5.4 retrieval + grounding-or-silence evaluation. These are REAL, documented in-flight anomalies from the crewed Apollo missions (7-12, 14-17; Apollo 13 is the reference corpus and is excluded). Rationale: the fleet shared hardware (CSM Block II, LM, Saturn V), so anomalies from other flights are faults our Apollo-13 procedures corpus has never indexed but whose hardware it shares. scope='in' (shared CSM/LM/Saturn subsystems) drives recall@k / completeness; scope='out' (mission-unique: LRV, ALSEP, EVA/EMU, SIM-bay experiments) drives honest-decline (grounding-or-silence). 'relevant' = the corpus segment ids a subject-matter reviewer judges SHOULD be retrieved for an in-scope query; it is intentionally EMPTY and must be filled BLIND to system output (see paper §5.4). For scope='out', relevant stays [] and expect_decline=true. Consuming code should read the 'scenarios' list.
_integrity_notes: All sources are NASA primary documents but remain <VERIFY> until confirmed against clean scans. Apollo 10/11/12 items were confirmed via APSR Appendix F (JSC-09423), whose per-item anomaly NUMBERS were partly OCR-garbled — cite these by mission-report number + Anomaly-Summary section, not by an App-F item number.
Saturn V launch-vehicle anomalies live in separate MSFC flight-evaluation reports (not the spacecraft anomaly summaries); the Apollo 12 launch-lightning event is captured via the CSM/spacecraft side.
Biomedical / crew-illness events are excluded (not hardware anomalies).
One candidate (Apollo 17 deep-core / LSPE drill) was left OUT as UNVERIFIED.
